_about: SWITCH IT (9 Nov 2026): the same idea, from an email to a friend to an essay. One version is right; one is still chatty; one is formal but holds a grammar slip.

items.e: Honestly, phones in class are a total nightmare – nobody listens to the teacher!
items.ok: It could be argued that phones in class distract students from the lesson.

no.t: Honestly, phones in class are a real problem because nobody listens.
no.why: Still chatty: honestly and nobody are email words. An essay uses a neutral frame like it could be argued that.

no.t: It could be argued what phones in class distract students from the lesson.
no.why: Argued is followed by that, not what.

items.t: Honestly → It could be argued that · a total nightmare → distract students · no exclamation mark

items.e: I reckon we get way too much homework these days.
items.ok: Many people believe that students are given too much homework nowadays.

no.t: I reckon students are given too much homework nowadays.
no.why: I reckon is spoken English. In an essay, report what people believe.

no.t: Many people believe that students are giving too much homework nowadays.
no.why: Students receive the homework, so it’s passive: are given.

items.t: I reckon → Many people believe that · we get → students are given · these days → nowadays

items.e: Loads of my mates do sport, and it’s great for them.
items.ok: A large number of young people play sport, which has clear benefits for their health.

no.t: Lots of my friends do sport, and it’s great for them.
no.why: Lots of, my friends and great keep it personal and chatty.

no.t: A large number of young people play sport, what has clear benefits for their health.
no.why: To point back to a whole idea, use which, not what.

items.t: loads of my mates → a large number of young people · and it’s great → which has clear benefits

items.e: But the thing is, school uniforms are kind of boring.
items.ok: However, it is true that school uniforms can limit students’ individuality.

no.t: But the thing is, school uniforms limit students’ individuality.
no.why: But the thing is is how we talk, not how we write. Start with However.

no.t: However, it is true that school uniforms can limiting students’ individuality.
no.why: After can, use the bare verb: can limit.

items.t: But the thing is → However, it is true that · kind of boring → limit individuality

items.e: If you ask me, tourists are ruining my town!
items.ok: In my view, tourism can damage small communities if it is not managed carefully.

no.t: If you ask me, tourism damages small communities.
no.why: If you ask me talks to a friend. In my view does the same job in an essay.

no.t: In my view, tourism can damage small communities if it will not be managed carefully.
no.why: After if, use the present: if it is not managed.

items.t: If you ask me → In my view · ruining my town → damage small communities · a condition makes it balanced

items.e: Basically, online lessons are cool ’cause you can stay in your PJs.
items.ok: One advantage of online learning is that students can study from home.

no.t: Basically, online learning is good because students can study from home.
no.why: Basically and good are too casual. Name the advantage instead.

no.t: One advantage of online learning is what students can study from home.
no.why: The advantage is that…, not what….

items.t: Basically… cool → One advantage of… is that · stay in your PJs → study from home

items.e: Sure, social media’s fun, but it eats up loads of your time.
items.ok: Although social media is entertaining, it can take up a great deal of time.

no.t: Sure, social media is entertaining, but it takes up a lot of time.
no.why: Sure is spoken. Although sets up the contrast in one formal sentence.

no.t: Despite social media is entertaining, it can take up a great deal of time.
no.why: Despite takes a noun or -ing (despite being entertaining). Before a subject and a verb, use although.

items.t: Sure…, but → Although · eats up loads of → take up a great deal of

items.e: So yeah, I’d say cars should be banned from the town centre.
items.ok: To sum up, I believe that cars should be banned from the town centre.

no.t: So yeah, I believe cars should be banned from the town centre.
no.why: So yeah is chat. To sum up tells the reader the conclusion has started.

no.t: To sum up, I believe that cars should banned from the town centre.
no.why: The passive needs be: should be banned.

items.t: So yeah, I’d say → To sum up, I believe that

items.e: Kids who read a lot get better marks, no doubt about it.
items.ok: There is evidence that children who read regularly tend to achieve better results.

no.t: Kids who read a lot definitely get better marks.
no.why: Kids and definitely sound chatty and too sure. An essay is careful: tend to.

no.t: There is evidence that children who read regularly tend achieving better results.
no.why: Tend is followed by to + verb: tend to achieve.

items.t: Kids → children · no doubt about it → there is evidence · get better marks → tend to achieve better results

items.e: My parents always say video games rot your brain, but that’s rubbish.
items.ok: Some people claim that video games are harmful; however, this is not always the case.

no.t: My parents say video games are harmful, but that’s not true.
no.why: My parents and that’s not true are personal. Report the view, then answer it.

no.t: Some people claim that video games are harmful; however, this is not always a case.
no.why: The fixed phrase is not always the case.

items.t: My parents always say → Some people claim · that’s rubbish → this is not always the case

items.e: Plus, cycling to school saves you a ton of money.
items.ok: Furthermore, cycling to school is a cheaper way to travel.

no.t: Plus, cycling to school saves a lot of money.
no.why: Plus is informal for adding a point. Use Furthermore or In addition.

no.t: Furthermore, cycling to school is a more cheap way to travel.
no.why: Cheap is a short word: cheaper, not more cheap.

items.t: Plus → Furthermore · saves you a ton of money → is a cheaper way to travel

items.e: Doing a part-time job is a great way to learn stuff, trust me.
items.ok: Having a part-time job allows teenagers to develop useful skills.

no.t: Having a part-time job is a great way to learn stuff.
no.why: Stuff is too vague and chatty for an essay. Name it: useful skills.

no.t: Having a part-time job allows teenagers develop useful skills.
no.why: Allow is followed by someone + to: allows teenagers to develop.

items.t: a great way to learn stuff → allows teenagers to develop useful skills · trust me → gone

items.e: Fast food’s everywhere now, so no wonder people are getting unhealthy.
items.ok: As fast food has become widely available, many people’s diets have become less healthy.

no.t: Fast food is everywhere now, so no wonder people are unhealthy.
no.why: No wonder is spoken. Show the cause with As… in one full sentence.

no.t: As fast food became widely available, many people’s diets have become less healthy.
no.why: For a change up to now, use the present perfect in both clauses: has become.

items.t: so no wonder → As… (the cause first) · everywhere now → has become widely available

items.e: Exams are super stressful – I can’t stand them!
items.ok: Exams can cause high levels of stress among students.

no.t: Exams are very stressful and students can’t stand them.
no.why: Can’t stand is a strong personal feeling. An essay states the effect.

no.t: Exams can cause high levels of stress between students.
no.why: Among is for a whole group; between is for two.

items.t: super stressful – I can’t stand them! → can cause high levels of stress among students

items.e: Anyway, I think the government should do something about it.
items.ok: In conclusion, it is essential that the government takes action.

no.t: Anyway, it is essential that the government takes action.
no.why: Anyway changes the subject in a chat. In conclusion closes an essay.

no.t: In conclusion, it is essential that the government takes an action.
no.why: Take action is a fixed phrase, with no article.

items.t: Anyway, I think → In conclusion, it is essential that · do something → take action

items.e: Learning a language is hard work, but it’s totally worth it.
items.ok: Although learning a language requires effort, the benefits are considerable.

no.t: Learning a language is hard work, but it’s totally worth it in the end.
no.why: Totally and worth it are chatty. Name what is worth it: the benefits.

no.t: Although learning a language requires effort, but the benefits are considerable.
no.why: Use although or but, never both in one sentence.

items.t: hard work, but totally worth it → Although… requires effort, the benefits are considerable

items.e: Lots of people think zoos are cruel, and I kind of agree.
items.ok: It is often argued that zoos are cruel, and there is some truth in this.

no.t: Lots of people think zoos are cruel, and I agree with them.
no.why: Lots of people think is chatty. It is often argued that is the essay frame.

no.t: It is often argued that zoos are cruel, and there is some true in this.
no.why: After some, use the noun: truth.

items.t: Lots of people think → It is often argued that · I kind of agree → there is some truth in this

items.e: Teachers should totally let us use our phones for research.
items.ok: Schools should allow students to use phones for research purposes.

no.t: Teachers should let students use their phones for research.
no.why: Let is fine in speech; allow… to is the essay word.

no.t: Schools should allow students using phones for research purposes.
no.why: Allow someone is followed by to + verb: allow students to use.

items.t: totally let us → allow students to · our phones → phones for research purposes

items.e: Nobody walks anywhere anymore – everyone’s glued to their cars.
items.ok: Fewer people walk than in the past, as many rely heavily on their cars.

no.t: Nobody walks anymore because everyone is glued to their cars.
no.why: Nobody and glued to are exaggerations. An essay is measured: fewer people.

no.t: Less people walk than in the past, as many rely heavily on their cars.
no.why: People can be counted, so use fewer, not less.

items.t: Nobody… anymore → Fewer people… than in the past · glued to → rely heavily on

items.e: What’s the point of learning history? It’s all in the past!
items.ok: Some students question the value of studying history.

no.t: What is the point of studying history?
no.why: A question to the reader can work in an article, but an essay states the view.

no.t: Some students question the value of study history.
no.why: After of, use -ing: the value of studying.

items.t: What’s the point…? → Some students question the value of… · a question becomes a statement
